I worked on that ship, almost 20 years ago. There was a fire on board a few weeks after I left, which turned out to be caused by some careless welding. I'm willing to bet this (latest incident) happened because someone didn't respect the maintenance tag on the switch shutting off power to the elevator motor, and started it up because of a complaint that it wasn't working. Quick turnaround and bodge jobs always won out over proper repairs. "We'll fix it in dry dock" was the mantra. (Every year they either did a one week wet dock or two week dry dock, alternating each year. Most repairs that were less than mission critical had to wait for those times.)

Bear in mind the way cruise ships work. When they get back to the home port, typically on a Sunday morning for a 7 day cruise, they discharge all the passengers. Meanwhile they're taking on supplies below, and offloading garbage. Starting around noon, the flow goes the other way, as they take on the new passengers, and at 4 to 5 pm, they sail away again. There is no down time to do things right, unless it can be done invisibly to the passengers. That's why this poor guy died – because his work was not invisible to the passengers, and someone got impatient.

"*Faster.*"

Exhausted, the Holnareem child loosened his grip on the sword and shield. His arms went slack as he took a breath of the dry air. A moment later, they tightened as he took up a fighting stance once more. Shadowy figures sprang to life around him, and began to close. Two moved in from either side in a pincer movement, while one dead ahead raised an ephemeral blade in challenge. The child stood frozen like a statue, neither preparing a defence nor moving to attack. A final shadow raised a knife for a killing blow to his back, and the moment had arrived.

The boy blurred from mortal sight as he lunged to the left. A sweep from the sword in his right hand, a jab to the throat from the sharpened shield in his left, and the two phantoms were sliced apart like so much silk. Without slowing, the child sank down and delivered a drop kick to the knee of another shadow. An audible crunch was heard as the knee imploded, and the boy's eyes widened - the master was not playing this time: these shadows had substance. Quickly he leapt back and returned to a guard stance. In just over a second he had mortally wounded two opponents and crippled another. Three remained to face him.

He knew it was not good enough.

Another lunge, and the closest shadow was eviscerated. He caught a jab from another on the edge of his shield and delivered a vicious counter strike to the eyes. The final enemy had time to raise a knife to throw before he bull-rushed it with raised shield. As it staggered, he delivered a backhand which twisted the creature's head entirely around. It dropped to the floor, and the child looked up to see his master looming over him.

"*Rezac, do you know what it is that you shall face outside this realm?*" the figure hissed. "*They will not be mere shadows, boy. You will face abominations the likes of which have never entered your darkest dreams. Monsters which can twist the shapings of the earth below your feet, creatures which can vanish before your eyes and kill you before your next heartbeat. You. Must. Move. Faster. Already your strength far surpasses my hopes, but against the foes which you must face strength is not enough.*"

The shadow turned away, dismissing him with a wave. "*You are exhausted. Rest for a day. When we resume training, you shall practice aerial combat.*"

Rezac bowed his head in obedience, and retreated from the training cave. Left to himself, Meranath smiled in the darkness. "*This one will make a fitting avatar indeed...*" he crooned.
